title: A modified approach to image guided cell based therapy for cardiovascular diseases using cardiac precursor nanoprobe - GloTrack
protocol: Anesthetize the C57BL/6 mice with 2.0% isoflurane and 0.6 L/min oxygen during induction.
Reduce the concentration of isoflurane to approximately 1.5 % during maintenance.
Dilute 50 mL of 10 X PBS without calcium and magnesium in 450 mL of autoclaved distilled water.
Adjust the pH of the diluted PBS solution to 7.4.
Reconstitute the lyophilized human SIRPα/CD172a antibody in 0.2 µm filtered PBS to a final concentration of 0.5 mg/mL.
Aliquot the reconstituted antibodies into sterile prelabeled 500 µL tubes and store at -20 °C for up to 6 months.
Reconstitute the lyophilized human VEGF R2/KDR/Flk-1 antibody in sterile PBS to a final concentration of 0.5 mg/mL.
Aliquot the reconstituted antibodies into pre-labeled 500 µL tubes and store at -20 °C for up to 6 months.
Dilute each sample in MilliQ water for dynamic light scattering analysis.
Carry out measurements in triplicates at 25 °C using the Malvern Zetasizer Nano ZS.
Connect the oxygen and isoflurane reservoir to the main induction system (SurgiVet, Highland Medical Equipment).
Connect the induction chamber, nose mask, and ventilator to the main system using appropriate tubing.
Deliver 1.5 – 2.0% isoflurane with 0.6 L/min oxygen.
Under sterile conditions, transfer 10 μL of commercially available iron oxide (II, II) magnetic nanoparticles into a 500 μL sterile centrifuge tube for mini GloTrack preparation.
Vortex the SPION containing bottle briefly prior to aspirating the desired volume of solution.
Centrifuge the aliquot of SPION suspension at 8000 rpm for 15 min at room temperature.
Under sterile conditions, carefully remove the supernatant and wash the SPION pellet with 100 µL of 70 % ethanol.
Re-centrifuge the SPION-ethanol suspension at 8000 rpm for 15 min at RT.
Aspirate out the supernatant under sterile conditions.
Open the flap of the centrifuge tubes in the laminar air flow to allow excess alcohol to evaporate from the tubes for 2 – 3 min.
Add 100 µL of PEG 300 (10 mg/mL) to functionalize the particles.
Close, label and seal the tubes tight with parafilm.
Allow the tubes to spin in a magnetically stirred water bath at room temperature for 16 h.
To the functionalized SPIONs suspension, add 5 µg/mL mouse anti-human monoclonal SIRPA/KDR unconjugated antibodies.
Incubate the antibodies with the PEGylated SPION at 4°C on a magnetically stirred water bath containing ice cold water for 2 hours to enhance binding.
Ensure the temperature of the water is maintained throughout the 2 h period.
Store the engineered GloTrack at -20°C.
Functionalize the SPION particles with PEG (10 mg/mL).
Add 5 μg/mL mouse anti-human monoclonal SIRPA conjugated with PE and mouse anti-human KDR unconjugated antibody to the functionalized SPION particles.
Incubate for 2 hours on a magnetically stirred water bath containing ice-cold water, foiled wrapped to avoid photo bleaching of fluorescence dyes.
Allow antibodies to bind to the open moieties of PEG at 4°C.
Add secondary goat anti-mouse FITC tagged antibody IgG at a 1:100 dilution to the GloTrack.
Incubate further for 30 minutes at 4°C in a magnetically stirred water bath containing ice-cold water.
Store the conjugate GloTrack at 4°C until samples are analyzed using confocal microscopy or flow cytometry for 1 – 2 days.
Transfer SPIONs, PEGylated SPION, and GloTrack into clean pre-labeled test tubes.
Place these pre-labeled test tubes into a beaker containing methanol of LR grade.
Fix the test tubes in place with cork and adhesive tapes to avoid cracks and leakages.
Transfer the beaker with samples and tubes into an ultrasonic bath and sonicate for 15 minutes.
Remove the test tubes carefully and transfer their contents onto pre-labeled clean Petri dishes.
Lift a 3mm mesh carbon coated copper grid using fine tip tweezers and place it on the sample to adsorb it.
Carefully place the carbon coated side of the grid by placing it on its side first, then gently lay it over the sample.
Transfer the sample-adsorbed grid onto a lint free paper.
Place the grid in front of an infrared light for drying for one minute.
Avoid excessive dryness as it will lead to artifact formation.
Reverse the sides of the grid every 15 sec for uniform drying.
Store infra red dried samples overnight in a vacuum desiccators for examination under electron microscope on the following day.
Examine the infra red dried samples using Tecnai 20 electron microscope without additional staining.
Mount the sample loaded carbon coated copper grid onto either a single or double tilt holder.
Use appropriate tweezers for loading samples and handle the grid with care to avoid flexing.
Place the grid loaded holder into the stage of the microscope as specified in the user operation manual.
Turn on the filament and using the Tecnai user interface open the column.
Adjust the translating track ball to bring the specimen inside the range of the image on the phosphorous screen and then adjust the eucentric height.
Focus the image on the screen.
Use well spread electron beams to avoid any damage to the samples.
Record an image of the area of interest using a CCD camera.
Label the images appropriately with the micron bars, kV and date using the digital software.
Provide the information to the system about the magnification to have the correct micron marker for more accurate measurement of size.
Reset the holder position after image capture.
Adjust the magnification to 4400X.
Centre and spread the beam to full screen.
Close the column valve.
Turn off the filament.
Remove the sample holder from the microscope.
Prepare samples for SEM as mentioned in Step 15 A i – vii.
Place the sample loaded carbon coated grid on the ion beam thinning (IBT) holder.
Secure the grid in the 3mm slot tightly to avoid drifting during imaging.
Vent the microscope.
Clean the microscope stage and place a fresh carbon tape for placing the samples.
Load and mount the specimen in the microscope carefully.
Pump the microscope to obtain the working vacuum level (~10^-5 torr).
Initialize the stage by setting the x, y and z axis to zero.
Turn on the extra high tension and set it between 5 – 10 kV.
Choose the secondary image mode and image at low magnification.
Locate the region of interest by focusing on the specimen surface.
Optimize imaging parameters such as working distance, filament current, aperture size, probe focus, brightness, and contrast for each sample.
Capture images in different areas of interest.
Capture images on high resolution and slow scan speed to obtain good resolution images.
Turn off the extra high tension.
Vent the microscope prior to removing the samples.
Pump the vacuum back again.
Handle the samples and grid with care to avoid damages.
Cut the glass slide to a 1mm x 1mm square using isomet on slow speed.
Clean the glass slide on either side with acetone in an ultrasonic cleaning machine for 15 minutes.
Fix the Teflon glue disc uniformly onto the glass slide, ensuring no air bubbles are present.
Take an aliquot of SPION, PEGylated SPION, and GloTrack samples into pre-labeled test tubes.
Place the pre-labeled test tubes in a beaker containing methanol.
Fix the test tubes in place with cork and cello tape.
Place the beaker in an ultrasonic cleaner and sonicate for 15 minutes.
Remove the test tubes from the sonicator.
Transfer a drop of the solution onto the Teflon glue disk on the glass slide.
Ensure uniform spread without air bubbles on the Teflon glue disk.
Place the samples under an infra red lamp for one minute.
Allow complete air drying in clean atmosphere.
Turn on the atomic force microscope, optical microscope, and computer on the anti-vibration table.
Open the interface and desired Nanonics software for acquisition.
Place the samples on the vibration-free piezo stage.
Choose the intermittent AFM mode.
Mount the tip on the upper scanner of the microscope.
Tune the frequency of the cantilever to match the frequency of the tuning fork as supplied by manufacturers.
Locate the set points.
Check the read error channel, which should preferably be 0.3.
Use the optical light microscope to determine the region of interest.
Focus on the tip of the region of interest using the X and Y movement of the stage.

Approach the AFM tip on the sample using the coarse approach with high speed (900Hz – 1250Hz) till the distance between the samples is 1 – 2 mm or alternatively with fine approach of 200 – 300 Hz under slow speed.
Ensure the engagement of the probe on the surface by both the hardware and software.
On the scanning probe microscope (SPM) controller, check for the illumination of the feedback (FB).
On the software, check for the fluctuation of the error signal needle around zero.
Pre-set all scan parameters including area, pixel size, dwell time, scan direction, location of scanner and also the scanner mode prior to beginning the scan.
Turn off the optical light to minimize sample drift before starting the scan.
Begin scanning the area of interest.
Check the image quality and save the file after capturing the images.
Convert the file to the required format for 2D and 3D surface image profiles when desired.
Use Nanonics software (v NWS11_1.0) to analyze the results for roughness, 2D and 3D surface topography, etc.
Transfer 20 µL of SPION into a clean and pre-labeled 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 500 µL of SPION PEG to the same tube.
Add 500 µL of GloTrack prepared with unconjugated antibodies to the tube.
Dilute the samples in each tube to a total volume of 1 mL using water.
Gently vortex the diluted samples prior to analysis.
Load the samples onto a 1 mL disposable syringe, avoiding air bubble formation.
Clean inside of the zeta cell thoroughly by flushing it with water, followed by ethanol and then with water.
Transfer the samples into a cuvette and fill between 10 – 15 mm in height.
Gently tap to remove any presence of air bubbles in the cuvette.
Place the cuvette in its slot in the machine.
Run the samples after loading the desired protocol preset in the machine.
Record the sample size values and histogram from the generated report following measurement.
Use the previously prepared sample for Zeta potential estimation and load it into the zeta cuvette.
Ensure the sample is filled completely in the cuvette, submerging the electrodes with equal levels on either side of the Zeta cell.
Clean the sides of the zeta cuvette and place it in its slot.
Run the samples in triplicates using a zeta protocol.
Generate histogram with acquired sample values from the measurement file summary.
Take an aliquot of 50 µL of SPION in a clean 500 µL tube.
Vortex the SPION suspension at high speed for 10 seconds.
Place an aliquot of 10 µL on a clean glass slide.
Allow it to partially air dry for 1-2 min.
Place a cover slip over the dried sample.
Fix the cover slip and seal edges to avoid disturbance during acquisition.
Take an aliquot of PEG coated SPION in a clean 500 µL foil wrapped tube.
Add goat anti mouse FITC to the PEG coated SPION at a ratio of 1:100.
Allow labeled antibody to non-specifically bind to open moieties for 30 min at 4°C.
Remove 10 µL of the labeled functionalized SPION and place on a clean pre-labeled slide.
Allow it to partially air dry.
Place a cover slip over the dried sample.
Seal edges of the cover slip.
Foil wrap the slides and store at 4°C for up to 2 days prior to imaging under confocal microscopy.
Bring the tubes containing fluorescent labeled GloTrack to room temperature.
Place an aliquot of the fluorescent labeled GloTrack mix on a glass slide in a dark room.
Allow the GloTrack mixture to partially air dry.
Place a glass cover slip over the aliquot.
Seal the edges of the glass cover slip.
Wait prior to observation.
Wrap the slides in foil and store at 4°C for up to 2 days before imaging under confocal microscopy.
Analyze SPION particles under transmission light.
Capture FITC labeled SPION-PEG images using 488 laser and transmission light.
Capture GloTrack images using 488 and 544 laser along with transmission light.
Transfer two aliquots of 50 µL of SPION each into two 500 µL centrifuge tubes.
Vortex the aliquots at high speed.
To one SPION aliquot, add 5 µL of FITC labeled goat anti mouse IgG.
Incubate in dark for 30 min.
Label the tubes appropriately and foil wrap the tube with the fluorescent dye.
Transfer two aliquots of SPION PEG each 250 µL into clean centrifuge tubes and vortex gently.
To one aliquot of the functionalized SPION add goat anti mouse IgG FITC secondary antibody.
Incubate in the dark for 30 min.
Label tube appropriately and foil wrap the tube with the fluorescent dye.
Take 250 µL of GloTrack prepared as explained in step 10 – 14.
Foil wrap the tube to avoid photobleaching and label accordingly.
Transfer 250 µL of GloTrack prepared as explained in steps 1-9 into a clean centrifuge tube.
After 30 mins of incubation in dark, transfer all the aliquots of SPION, SPION PEG and GloTrack into pre-labeled FACS tubes.
Make up the volume to 500 µL with PBS.
Label these individual tubes with their corresponding sample names and treat as test groups.
Vortex each of these samples prior to acquiring.
Transfer all the aliquots of SPION, SPION PEG and GloTrack into fresh, clean FACS tubes.
Make up the volume of each to 500 µL with PBS.
Label these individual tubes with the corresponding sample name and retain as controls.
Set the FACS machine as per the manufacturer’s instructions.
Carry out the analysis using the Cell Quest software.
Acquire the control unconjugated SPION, SPION PEG and GloTrack samples initially at low voltage.
Adjust the peaks for FITC and PE dyes by altering voltages.
Align the positive and negative regions carefully while adjusting voltages.
Set the protocol upon completing the adjustments.
Run the remaining conjugated SPIN, SPION PEG and GloTrack samples.
Save the data of each sample.
Anesthetize C57BL6 mice with 1.5 – 2 % isoflurane and 0.6 L/min oxygen in the induction chamber.
Observe for relaxed muscles and absence of pedal, palpebral and corneal reflexes to confirm complete sedation.
Use a mouse tail illuminator (MIL) to highlight the tail veins.
Insert a 23 gauge needle and one French catheter for venipuncture prior to inserting a tail vein catheter into anesthetized mice.
Ensure the catheter is in place.
Tape the mouse tail in place using HY-TAPE around the catheter and tail.
Restrain the anesthetized mouse and place it within the MR probe.
Maintain the temperature of the imaging scanner at 37 ºC.
Position the animal in a supine position with the head first.
Pre-scan the animals prior to administering GloTrack to obtain baseline values.
Resuspend GloTrack in saline to bring it to a final concentration of 1 mg/Kg body weight.
Administer 100 µL of resuspended GloTrack through the tail vein using a 1mL syringe.
Take a series of images over a 90 min period to determine the kinetic distribution of GloTrack to different tissue parts.
Carry out post-processing of the images using Paravision v5.1 software (Bruker Biospin).

Generate a differential image (post-contrast minus pre-contrast image data set for the same slice) to determine the migration and entrapment of GloTrack in different locations based on the decrease of MR signal intensity.
Statistically analyze the data using ANOVA for migration kinetics.
Use Student’s t-test for MRI signal intensities in measured tissues (e.g., heart, kidneys, lung, liver, muscle).
